-- The TARGET is these definitions, which also appear in the context: d14
def d14 (N : S1 X Y) (T : ℕ) : S1 X Y where
  A1 := Fin T × N.A1
  a2 := inferInstance
  A3 := fun a => N.A3 a.2
  a4 := fun a => N.a4 a.2
  a5 := fun a σ x =>
    N.a5 a.2 (fun m => if h : a.1.val = 0 then N.a4 m else σ (⟨a.1.val - 1, by omega⟩, m)) x
  a6 := fun σ =>
    if h : T = 0 then N.a6 N.a4 else N.a6 (fun m => σ (⟨T - 1, by omega⟩, m))
translation: Inside namespace S1, for any types X and Y (implicit), S1.d14 is a definition that takes a structure N of type S1 X Y and a natural number T (with no additional hypotheses on X, Y, N, or T) and constructs a new structure of type S1 X Y with the following fields: (1) A1 is the product type Fin T × N.A1, consisting of pairs a = (a.1, a.2) where a.1 is a natural number in {0, ..., T - 1} (empty if T = 0) and a.2 is in N.A1. (2) a2 is the automatically inferred Fintype instance proving that Fin T × N.A1 is finite. (3) A3 assigns to each pair a in Fin T × N.A1 the type N.A3 a.2 (depending only on the second component). (4) a4 assigns to each pair a in Fin T × N.A1 the element N.a4 a.2 of N.A3 a.2 (depending only on the second component). (5) a5 takes a pair a in Fin T × N.A1, a dependent function σ : (b : Fin T × N.A1) → N.A3 b.2, and an element x of X, and returns N.a5 a.2 f x in N.A3 a.2, where f : (m : N.A1) → N.A3 m sends each m in N.A1 to N.a4 m if a.1.val = 0 (ignoring σ), and otherwise sends m to σ (⟨a.1.val - 1, _⟩, m) (evaluating σ at the pair whose first component is a.1.val - 1 in Fin T and whose second component is m). (6) a6 takes a dependent function σ : (b : Fin T × N.A1) → N.A3 b.2 and returns an element of Y: if T = 0, it returns N.a6 N.a4 (ignoring σ); if T ≠ 0, it returns N.a6 applied to the function sending each m in N.A1 to σ (⟨T - 1, _⟩, m) (evaluating σ at the pair whose first component is T - 1 in Fin T and whose second component is m).

divergences.description: Pipelined real-time execution versus one-shot sequential unrolling (declared by the author): [P-H10] describes standard unrolling through time, where copy k is evaluated once for timestep k and feeds its output into copy k+1. In d14, all T copies operate in parallel as a synchronous pipeline inside S1 X Y: every copy updates at every step, every copy receives the current input x, every copy is initialized to N.a4, copy 0 always computes from N.a4, and the output is always read from copy T - 1 (relying on 1-step inter-layer state propagation). This changes the evaluation mechanism but preserves acyclicity, the T-fold copy structure, layer k+1 computing from layer k, and T-step input-output equivalence.

Abstract finite-node state machine versus neural networks: [P-D52a] and [P-H10] discuss unrolling recurrent neural networks (e.g., as in LeCun et al., 2015, and discretizing continuous time into discrete timesteps). In Lean, d14 unrolls an abstract discrete-time synchronous machine (S1 X Y) with arbitrary node state types and arbitrary transition and readout functions, omitting neural-network specifics such as weights, activation functions, and continuous-time discretization.

Finite-horizon and edge-case handling: d14 is parametrized by a finite horizon T : ℕ (matching [P-H10], while making explicit a finite-horizon restriction left implicit in [P-D52a]), and because d14 N T still accepts arbitrarily long input lists, beyond T steps it behaves as a T-step sliding-window machine rather than halting or being restricted to T steps. In the degenerate case T = 0, there is no last copy, so a6 bypasses the network state and returns the hardcoded value N.a6 N.a4.

judgement.summary: The Lean definition d14 accurately implements the author's declared real-time pipelined variant of unrolling through time, preserving the core structural properties of [P-D52a] and [P-H10] (T copies of the network, strictly feedforward dependencies from copy k to copy k+1, and T-step equivalence). Its differences from the source passages—the synchronous pipelined execution with broadcast inputs and shared initial states, the abstract state-machine formalism, and the T = 0 and post-horizon behaviors—are minor adaptations rather than material distortions.
